1012:        # Deliberately do NOT use --nooverlap: each identity owns a distinct
1013:        # read-only block-device view of the SAME partition, with no copies.
1014:        seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
1015:        seed_record_loops
1016:    fi
1017:    if [ -n "$leaf_loop" ]; then
1018:        seed_verify_loop "$leaf_loop" "$leaf" 0
1019:    else
1020:        [ -z "$(losetup -j "$leaf" -n -O NAME)" ] || seed_fail "leaf already mapped outside its receipt"
1021:        leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
1022:        seed_record_loops
1023:    fi
1024:    [ "$seed_view" != "$leaf_loop" ] || seed_fail "identical seed and leaf devices"
1025:}
1026:seed_verify_volume() {
1027:    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
1028:        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
1029:        [ "$(seed_super "$leaf_loop")" = "$sprout_fsid" ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout mount"
1030:    members=$(btrfs filesystem show --raw "$seed_dir/volume")
1031:    printf '%s\n' "$members" | grep -q "uuid: $sprout_fsid" || seed_fail "mounted FSID differs"
1032:    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {n++} END {print n+0}')" = 2 ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout member count"
1033:    actual_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {print $NF}' | sort)
1034:    expected_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$seed_view" "$leaf_loop" | sort)
1035:    [ "$actual_members" = "$expected_members" ] || seed_fail "sprout members differ from own loop receipts"
1036:}
1037:seed_member_pin() {
1038:    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || seed_fail "missing or unsafe sibling subvolume: $1"
1039:    pin_show=$(btrfs subvolume show "$1") || seed_fail "not a subvolume: $1"
1040:    pin_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "Subvolume" && $2 == "ID:" {print $3}')
1041:    pin_uuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "UUID:" {print $2}')
1042:    printf '%s' "$pin_id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$' && [ "$pin_id" -gt 5 ] && valid_session "$pin_uuid" || seed_fail "invalid sibling subvolume identity"
1043:    jq -cn --arg id "$pin_id" --arg uuid "$pin_uuid" '{id:$id,uuid:$uuid}'
1044:}
1045:seed_layout_pins() {
1046:    # Listing at subvolid=5 includes nested members. Do not merely check that
1047:    # the seven expected names exist: reject every extra or nested subvolume.
1048:    subvolume_listing=$(btrfs subvolume list "$seed_dir/volume") || seed_fail "cannot enumerate seed subvolumes"
1049:    actual_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' "$subvolume_listing" | sed -n 's/^.* path //p' | LC_ALL=C sort)
1050:    expected_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user | LC_ALL=C sort)
1051:    [ "$actual_subvolumes" = "$expected_subvolumes" ] || seed_fail "seed must contain exactly seven flat sibling subvolumes"
1052:    [ ! -e "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] && [ ! -L "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] || seed_fail "old extra persistence subvolume/layout is unsupported"
1053:    pins='{}'
1054:    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
1055:        pin=$(seed_member_pin "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling") || seed_fail "cannot pin sibling: $sibling"
1056:        pins=$(printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -c --arg member "$sibling" --argjson pin "$pin" '. + {($member):$pin}') || seed_fail "cannot record sibling pin"
1057:    done
1058:    printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -ce 'select(([.[].id] | unique | length) == 7 and ([.[].uuid] | unique | length) == 7)'
1059:}
1060:seed_persist_pin() {
1061:    persist_parent=$seed_dir/volume/@agent_user
1062:    persist_dir=$persist_parent/persist
1063:    parent_pin=$(seed_member_pin "$persist_parent") || seed_fail "invalid persistence parent"
1064:    [ -d "$persist_dir" ] && [ ! -L "$persist_dir" ] &&
1065:        [ "$(stat -c %a "$persist_dir")" = 700 ] || seed_fail "unsafe ordinary persistence directory"
1066:    ! btrfs subvolume show "$persist_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || seed_fail "persistence must not be a subvolume"
1067:    ! mountpoint -q "$persist_dir" || seed_fail "persistence source must not be a separate mount"
1068:    [ "$(stat -c %d "$persist_dir")" = "$(stat -c %d "$persist_parent")" ] || seed_fail "persistence is not on its parent filesystem"
1069:    # The sprout FSID identifies the device set across remounts. Kernel st_dev
1070:    # is checked against the parent live, never persisted as a reboot-stable ID.
1071:    jq -cn --argjson parent "$parent_pin" --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$persist_dir")" --arg fsid "$sprout_fsid" \
1072:        '{path:"@agent_user/persist",parent:$parent,inode:$inode,fsid:$fsid}'
1073:}
1074:seed_verify_layout() {
1075:    [ "$(seed_image_metadata | jq -cS .)" = "$(jq -cS '.image' "$seed_dir/state.json")" ] || seed_fail "pinned image metadata changed"
1076:    actual_pins=$(seed_layout_pins) || seed_fail "invalid shared sibling layout"

seed_attach() {
    # Serialize shared-seed alias registration across identities. Keep this
    # stable host lock separate from per-identity receipts/Cozo authority.
    seed_shared_lock
    # Same-boot missing/reassigned mappings require operator inspection.
    # Cross-boot receipts are cleared only by seed_load's verified cold gate.
    if [ -n "$seed_view" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$seed_view" "$seed_device" 1
    else
        # Deliberately do NOT use --nooverlap: each identity owns a distinct
        # read-only block-device view of the SAME partition, with no copies.
        seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    if [ -n "$leaf_loop" ]; then
        seed_verify_loop "$leaf_loop" "$leaf" 0
    else
        [ -z "$(losetup -j "$leaf" -n -O NAME)" ] || seed_fail "leaf already mapped outside its receipt"
        leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
        seed_record_loops
    fi
    [ "$seed_view" != "$leaf_loop" ] || seed_fail "identical seed and leaf devices"
}
seed_verify_volume() {
    [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
        [ "$(findmnt -rn -M "$seed_dir/volume" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
        [ "$(seed_super "$leaf_loop")" = "$sprout_fsid" ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout mount"
    members=$(btrfs filesystem show --raw "$seed_dir/volume")
    printf '%s\n' "$members" | grep -q "uuid: $sprout_fsid" || seed_fail "mounted FSID differs"
    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {n++} END {print n+0}')" = 2 ] || seed_fail "unexpected sprout member count"
    actual_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$members" | awk '$1 == "devid" {print $NF}' | sort)
    expected_members=$(printf '%s\n' "$seed_view" "$leaf_loop" | sort)
    [ "$actual_members" = "$expected_members" ] || seed_fail "sprout members differ from own loop receipts"
}
seed_member_pin() {
    [ -d "$1" ] && [ ! -L "$1" ] || seed_fail "missing or unsafe sibling subvolume: $1"
    pin_show=$(btrfs subvolume show "$1") || seed_fail "not a subvolume: $1"
    pin_id=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "Subvolume" && $2 == "ID:" {print $3}')
    pin_uuid=$(printf '%s\n' "$pin_show" | awk '$1 == "UUID:" {print $2}')
    printf '%s' "$pin_id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$' && [ "$pin_id" -gt 5 ] && valid_session "$pin_uuid" || seed_fail "invalid sibling subvolume identity"
    jq -cn --arg id "$pin_id" --arg uuid "$pin_uuid" '{id:$id,uuid:$uuid}'
}
seed_layout_pins() {
    # Listing at subvolid=5 includes nested members. Do not merely check that
    # the seven expected names exist: reject every extra or nested subvolume.
    subvolume_listing=$(btrfs subvolume list "$seed_dir/volume") || seed_fail "cannot enumerate seed subvolumes"
    actual_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' "$subvolume_listing" | sed -n 's/^.* path //p' | LC_ALL=C sort)
    expected_subvolumes=$(printf '%s\n' @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user | LC_ALL=C sort)
    [ "$actual_subvolumes" = "$expected_subvolumes" ] || seed_fail "seed must contain exactly seven flat sibling subvolumes"
    [ ! -e "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] && [ ! -L "$seed_dir/volume/@persist" ] || seed_fail "old extra persistence subvolume/layout is unsupported"
    pins='{}'
    for sibling in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
        pin=$(seed_member_pin "$seed_dir/volume/$sibling") || seed_fail "cannot pin sibling: $sibling"
        pins=$(printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -c --arg member "$sibling" --argjson pin "$pin" '. + {($member):$pin}') || seed_fail "cannot record sibling pin"
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$pins" | jq -ce 'select(([.[].id] | unique | length) == 7 and ([.[].uuid] | unique | length) == 7)'

seed_persist_pin() {
    persist_parent=$seed_dir/volume/@agent_user
    persist_dir=$persist_parent/persist
    parent_pin=$(seed_member_pin "$persist_parent") || seed_fail "invalid persistence parent"
    [ -d "$persist_dir" ] && [ ! -L "$persist_dir" ] &&
        [ "$(stat -c %a "$persist_dir")" = 700 ] || seed_fail "unsafe ordinary persistence directory"
    ! btrfs subvolume show "$persist_dir" >/dev/null 2>&1 || seed_fail "persistence must not be a subvolume"

    [ "$(stat -c %d "$persist_dir")" = "$(stat -c %d "$persist_parent")" ] || seed_fail "persistence is not on its parent filesystem"

    jq -cn --argjson parent "$parent_pin" --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$persist_dir")" --arg fsid "$sprout_fsid" \

seed_verify_layout() {

## 4. Why the seed contract needs block storage
…

- A subvolume path is not the writable block member passed to `btrfs device add`.
- A writable snapshot of a read-only subvolume can isolate file changes, but **substituting it for a sprout changes the specified mechanism and proof model**.
- Keeping a backing file inside a subvolume still requires some block-device presentation for that file. Recording it in Cozo does not provide that presentation.
- A real non-loop block device can be added; a loop is an implementation choice, not a Btrfs requirement.

### Upgrade replica is a different issue

Btrfs send/receive operates on subvolumes and snapshots. There is no general Btrfs requirement that an upgrade replica occupy a second partition.

Upstream says:

> “All snapshots involved in one send command must be read-only…”

and:

> “Read-only mount of the subvolume is not sufficient…”

The receive documentation also requires protecting the receive destination against concurrent modification until reception completes.

Sources: [btrfs-send](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-send.html), [btrfs-receive](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/btrfs-receive.html).

**However, the supplied implementation currently requires more than that general primitive:** its V4 proof requires a separate upgrade filesystem, top-level mount, a single-device filesystem, GPT geometry, and a loop-backed second partition. Replacing that with a custom filesystem subvolume requires an explicit proof/schema migration, not a path substitution.

Citation: `evidence/source/crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/identity_clean_provision/partitioned.rs:109-138`.

---

## 5. Kernel 6.17+ and the permanent seed mount

The upstream caveat is exact:

> “Before v6.17 kernel, a seed device could have been mounted independently along with sprouted filesystems. But since 6.17 kernel, a seed device can only be mounted either through a sprouted filesystem, or the seed device itself, not both at the same time.”

Its reason:

> “This is to ensure a block device to have only a single filesystem bound to it, so that runtime device missing events can be properly handled.”

Source: [Btrfs seeding-device documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).

This applies directly to the **same-block-device** interpretation of the supplied 6.18 receipt and permanent standalone mount requirement.

It does **not** authorize:

- Unmounting the permanent seed.
- Clearing its seeding flag.
- Removing the seed from sprouts.
- Rebuilding/copying the seed.
- Downgrading or modifying the kernel.
- Assuming that aliases preserve supported sharing semantics.

The documentation itself warns that clearing the seeding flag and changing the seed invalidates existing dependent filesystems.

The contemporary maintainer discussion also explicitly discusses only one sprout mount at a time on the same device, but is a discussion rather than proof of every alias topology.  
Source: [August 2025 upstream filesystem discussion](https://www.spinics.net/lists/linux-fsdevel/msg309379.html).

**Do not combine the generic multi-sprout example with the version caveat to claim unrestricted concurrent same-device mounting on 6.18. Conversely, do not turn the caveat into an unsupported impossibility claim about every distinct block-view implementation.**

---

## 6. What actually worked historically—and what differs now

### October 5: native Incus plus external sprout construction

Historical `op-identity-root` creates distinct read-only seed loops and writable leaf loops:

```sh
seed_view=$(losetup --find --show --read-only --loop-ref "seed:$native_uuid" "$seed_device")
```

```sh
leaf_loop=$(losetup --find --show --loop-ref "leaf:$native_uuid" "$leaf")
```

It then performs:

```sh
btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
```

and binds the prepared filesystem root:

```sh
mount --bind "$guest" "$native_root"
```

Citations:

- `evidence/history/oct05-admission-helper/deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/op-identity-root:1003-1024`
- Same file `:1104-1124`
- Same file `:1147-1198`

It explicitly rejects a standalone physical-source mount:

> `directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto`

Citation: same file `:494-505`.

**Conclusion:** strong evidence that native Incus and sprouts were integrated, but this historical implementation violates the latest no-host-loops constraint and conflicts with the standalone permanent-mount requirement.

### October 11: upgrade-over-seed read-only root

The historical binder contains:

```sh
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$root/@" "$seed_layer"
mount --bind -o ro,X-mount.idmap=b:0:1000000:1000000000 "$replica/@" "$upgrade_layer"
mount -t overlay overlay -o "ro,lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer" "$view"
mount --bind "$view" "$container_root"
```

Citation: `evidence/history/oct11-start/deploy/scripts/bind-instance-root.sh:82-85`.

Important distinctions:

- Upgrade is the higher-priority **lower**.
- The other lower is the sprout’s inherited `@`.
- Root is read-only.
- There is no writable OverlayFS `upperdir`/`workdir`.
- Persistent identity writes live in separately bound inherited siblings and `@agent_user/persist`.

The supplied historical handoff states:

> “Canonical identity_sled.touch_session completed: 3tchedChatbot Running, PID11719.”

It also explicitly limits the persistence claim:

> “Boot wiring is deployed; actual reboot/cold-sync path unexercised…”

Citation: `evidence/context/HANDOFF.md:5940-5962`.

#!/bin/sh
# Host storage owner: remount/receive existing GPT members, never mint/start.
set -eu
fail() { printf 'restore-chatbot-root: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
check_only=false
if [ "${1:-}" = --check ]; then check_only=true; shift; fi
[ "$#" -le 1 ] || fail 'usage: restore-chatbot-root [--check] [NAME]'
name=${1:-3tchedCtlChatbot}
printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$' && [ "${#name}" -le 63 ] || fail 'invalid chatbot selector'
# The name selects the native target; the same existing UUID/session/key and
# storage receipts below are required for both the legacy alias and ID-N.
[ "$(id -u)" = 0 ] || fail 'host root required'
sid=b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28
key=[REDACTED:opaque-base64]
pool=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/3tched-pool
receipt=$pool/.provisioning/$name.boot.json
binding=$pool/.provisioning/$name.incus.json
disk=$pool/.provisioning/$name.json
root=/var/lib/incus/storage-pools/identity-roots/containers/$name/rootfs
view=$pool/.mounts/$name/root-view
seed_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/seed-layer
upgrade_layer=$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade-layer
readback() { timeout --kill-after=5s 30s "$@"; }
secure_path() (
    path=$1
    [ "$(realpath -e -- "$path")" = "$path" ] || fail "noncanonical path: $path"
    while :; do
        [ ! -L "$path" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u -- "$path")" = 0 ] &&
            [ $((0$(stat -c %a -- "$path") & 022)) -eq 0 ] || fail "unsafe owner/mode: $path"
        [ "$path" != / ] || break
        path=$(dirname -- "$path")
    done
)
secure_path "$pool"
[ "$(stat -c %u:%g "$pool")" = 0:0 ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSTYPE)" = btrfs ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o FSROOT)" = / ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$pool" -o UUID)" = a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] &&
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M / -o UUID)" != a1ab7b42-12a8-437c-8f65-d0469892c8dd ] ||
    fail 'canonical loop pool is not mounted on its pinned filesystem'
secure_path "$pool/.provisioning"
[ -d "$pool/.provisioning" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$pool/.provisioning")" = 0:0:700 ] ||
    fail 'preparation receipt directory must be private'
for file in "$receipt" "$binding" "$disk"; do
    secure_path "$file"
    [ -f "$file" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u:%g:%a "$file")" = 0:0:600 ] || fail "unsafe preparation receipt: $file"
done
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and
    .identity_registered==true and .restore_existing_pair==true
' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail 'chatbot boot attestation differs'

# existing native UUID/session/key and storage paths before any mount action.
jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$sid" --arg key "$key" --arg root "$root" --arg view "$view" '
    .version==1 and .name==$name and .session_id==$sid and .phase=="root-bound" and
    .root_bound==true and .root_view_readonly==true and .upgrade_paired==true and
    .threetched_root==$root and .root_view==$view and .instance.name==$name and .instance.type=="container" and
    .instance.config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .instance.config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    (.instance.config["volatile.uuid"]|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$"))

    (has("instance_uuid")|not) or .instance_uuid==$uuid

    --arg upgrade "$pool/.mounts/$name/upgrade" '
    .name==$name and .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
    .filesystem_prepared==true and .image==$image and .root_mount==$root and .upgrade_mount==$upgrade
' "$disk" >/dev/null || fail 'disk preparation pins differ'
image=$pool/$name.img
secure_path "$image"
[ -f "$image" ] && [ "$(stat -c %i "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_inode "$disk")" ] &&
    [ "$(stat -c %s "$image")" = "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$disk")" ] || fail 'image pins differ'
instance=$(readback incus --force-local query "/1.0/instances/$name?project=default") || fail 'native instance readback failed'

    .name==$name and .type=="container" and .config["volatile.uuid"]==$uuid and
    .config["user.opdbus.session_id"]==$sid and .config["user.opdbus.wireguard_public_key"]==$key and
    .config["security.privileged"]=="false" and .config["security.protection.shift"]=="true" and
    .config["boot.autostart"]=="false" and .profiles==["3tched-lungs"] and
    .devices.root.type=="disk" and .devices.root.path=="/" and .devices.root.pool=="identity-roots" and
    ((.status=="Stopped" and .status_code==102) or (.status=="Running" and .status_code==103))
' >/dev/null || fail 'native chatbot UUID/session/key/policy differs'
state=$(printf '%s\n' "$instance" | jq -er .status)
# Select the activated closure deliberately. When invoked from a source or
# received release, use that helper's sibling; never fall through to base copies.
self=$(realpath -e -- "$0") || fail 'cannot resolve restore helper'
helper_dir=$(dirname -- "$self")
case "$helper_dir" in
    /usr/local/libexec/3tched)
        helper_dir=/usr/local/libexec/op-dbus/helpers ;;
esac
sync_helper=$helper_dir/sync-instance-upgrade
case "$self" in
    */deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/restore-chatbot-root)
        sync_helper=$helper_dir/../../scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh ;;
esac
sync_helper=$(realpath -e -- "${OP_SYNC_INSTANCE_UPGRADE_HELPER:-$sync_helper}") || fail 'selected sync helper absent'
secure_path "$sync_helper"
[ -f "$sync_helper" ] && [ -x "$sync_helper" ] || fail 'selected sync helper not executable'
if [ "$state" = Running ]; then
    # A service restart observes only; it must not replace a running guest's lowers.
    [ "$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FSTYPE)" = overlay ] || fail 'running root is not overlay'
    options=$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o FS-OPTIONS) || fail 'cannot inspect running root'
    case ",$options," in *,"lowerdir=$upgrade_layer:$seed_layer",*) ;; *) fail 'running root lower pins differ' ;; esac
    case ",$(readback findmnt -rn -M "$root" -o VFS-OPTIONS)," in *,ro,*) ;; *) fail 'running root is not read-only' ;; esac
    exit 0
fi
[ "$check_only" != true ] || exit 0
exec "$sync_helper" boot "$name"

    gpt_name=$name
    selected_sessions="$selected_sessions$chatbot_session|"
done
for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
    physical_present=1
    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
    marker=$physical/$name/boot-ready.json
    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
        continue
    fi
    private_receipt "$receipt" && private_receipt "$marker" || fail "unsafe physical boot receipts: $name"
    # Keep existing canonical UUID roots. Both chatbot name forms require the
    # same pinned session and complete boot/storage receipt; neither grants identity.
    jq -e --arg name "$name" --arg sid "$chatbot_session" '
        .version==1 and .layout=="shared-partition-siblings-v2" and .name==$name and .phase=="ready" and
        (.session|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")) and
        (.instance_uuid|type=="string" and test("^[0-9a-f]{8}(-[0-9a-f]{4}){3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")) and
        (.session==$name or (.session==$sid and
            ($name|test("^(3tchedCtlChatbot|3tchedChatbot|ID-[1-9][0-9]*)$") and length<=63)))
    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null || fail "invalid/incomplete physical boot receipt: $name"
    policy=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot|select(type=="boolean")|tostring' "$marker") || fail "invalid physical boot policy: $name"
    expected=$(jq -cS --argjson start "$policy" '{version,layout,image,members,persist,name,session,instance_uuid,root,seed_fsid,seed_generation,sprout_fsid,leaf,leaf_inode,leaf_size,start_on_boot:$start}' "$receipt") || fail "invalid storage pins: $name"

    case "$selected_sessions" in

    physical_names="$physical_names $name"
done
failed=0
if [ -n "$gpt_name" ]; then
    "$restore_helper" "$gpt_name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
seed_readonly_ready=0
for name in $physical_names; do
    receipt=$physical/$name/state.json
    marker=$physical/$name/boot-ready.json
    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot|select(type=="boolean")|tostring' "$marker") || fail "invalid boot policy: $name"

    # session/key binding again under its lifecycle lock before touching roots.
    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then

        seed_readonly_ready=1
    fi
    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
    case "$state" in
        Running)
            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then
                "$helper" seed-lungs "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;
        Stopped)
            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
            ;;

            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
    esac
done
if [ "$physical_present" -eq 1 ] || [ "$gpt_present" -eq 1 ]; then
    # Never select legacy `up`: directly mounting the same seed conflicts with
    # retained sprouts even when another identity's root failed restoration.
    for image in "$legacy"/*/identity.img; do

        name=$(basename "$(dirname "$image")")
        case "$selected_sessions" in
            *"|$name|"*) echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by selected boot receipt"; continue ;;
        esac
        if { [ "$name" = 3tchedChatbot ] || [ "$name" = 3tchedCtlChatbot ]; } && [ "$gpt_present" -eq 1 ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by GPT boot receipt"
        elif [ -e "$physical/$name/state.json" ] || [ -L "$physical/$name/state.json" ]; then
            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
        else
            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
            failed=$((failed + 1))
        fi
    done
else
    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
fi
[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || fail "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed"
"$helper_dir/runit-ready-signal" identity-roots || exit 1
exec sleep infinity

## Architecture and historical differences
…
### 2. Oct5: true shared physical seed, but loop-backed private sprout
…
and, after pinning the inherited layout and rechecking physical-seed properties:

```sh
seed_write '.phase="device-add-intent"'
btrfs device add "$leaf_loop" "$seed_dir/volume"
```

**Citation:** A:same path`:1155-1198`.

Important semantics:

- The code deliberately does **not** copy or snapshot the root during sprout creation.
- The physical seed remains SEEDING and block-read-only.
- The writable leaf is a **block member**, not an OverlayFS upper.
- The inherited layout is exactly `@`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`, `@agent_shared`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_soul`, `@agent_user`.
- `@agent_user/persist` is an ordinary protected directory, not an eighth subvolume.
- Oct5 protects rules/shared/soul read-only; Oct11 changes rules to writable.
- `seed-up` restores mappings/mounts; `seed-down` detaches owned mappings. Neither is a license to repeat device-add.
- The helper pins loop ownership through native-UUID loop references and boot-aware receipts.

**Citations:** A:same path`:1045-1122,1217-1222,1260-1303`.

The historical helper also explicitly refuses a standalone direct mount of the physical seed:

```sh
seed_fail "directly mounted seed source; unmount it and keep its fstab entry noauto"
```

**Citation:** A:same path`:494-505`.

That is a historical behavior, **not an instruction to unmount today’s seed**. It conflicts with retaining a permanently mounted seed if that is part of the current required design.

#### Intended Oct5 completion chain

The wrapper prepares external host storage/native definition, submits a digest-pinned clean plan, reads back the authoritative binding, checks physical storage, starts through `identity_sled.touch_session`, reads authoritative/native state again, then publishes boot completion.

Original source:

```sh
# Canonical lifecycle admission verifies storage, starts the native guest
# and commits its active session state; native start alone is insufficient.
```

**Citation:** A:`deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh:354-384`.

This is an intended completion protocol; it does not establish that the historical run reached its end.

### 3. Oct11: GPT root/upgrade separation and manual staging

B’s wrapper explicitly distinguishes its new staged path from the retained unpartitioned workflow:

> “Existing identity mode below remains the older unpartitioned leaf workflow; do not pass a partitioned image to that mode.”

**Citation:** B:`deploy/scripts/pro

# Upgrade overlay specification

Task: `provisioning-fusion-20261019` · 2026-10-19 · Status: specification only.

## Ownership and decision

The owner implements the known-working provisioning baseline and supplies its interface and authoritative receipts. Fusion specifies **only the upgrade overlay** in the existing `sync-instance-upgrade.sh` → `bind-instance-root.sh` / `restore-chatbot-root` → `identity-roots` workflow. This document does not claim that the owner has completed the baseline.

Retain a separate Btrfs send/receive upgrade replica. Compose the root read-only with **upgrade above inherited seed root**, without `upperdir` or `workdir`. Bind ordinary private persistence separately. Preserve caller/session, existing native UUID, immutable seed, inherited siblings, admission, idmap and authoritative receipts. No new orchestrator, grants, identity/container creation, provisioning-proof changes or backing selection.

No host loops remains mandatory, including restoration paths. The owner supplies the established backing and restoration interface; this specification neither selects it nor claims a proven no-image topology. Earlier broad proposals about provisioning/proof migration are outside this scope. Pending owner integration values are a handoff dependency, not a newly discovered architectural blocker.

## Evidence and current implementation

Citations `S:` below are relative to `../evidence/source/`; `R:` to `../recovery/`. They are saved source evidence, not live readiness receipts. Read-only SHA-256 comparison against the current checkout found `identity-roots/run` byte-identical; diffs for sync, bind and restore found only the export's redacted public-key literal. Thus the cited overlay behavior also exists in the inspected current checkout. Installed/runtime equality was not checked.

| Existing part | Evidence | Narrow remaining work |
|---|---|---|
| Host/instance locks, stopped native UUID/session validation, bounded observations, durable send intent | S: `deploy/scripts/sync-instance-upgrade.sh:42-114,203-239,281-284` | Consume owner handoff; coordinate with existing lifecycle exclusion, not merely helper-local locks. |
| Full initial send; later incremental send from retained read-only parent; received UUID equals sent UUID | S: sync `155-169,329-337` | Bind parent and candidate to exact generation identities; revalidate destination immediately before receive. |
| Immutable received baseline plus separate published clone; clone parent UUID checked | S: sync `338-346,394-405` | Record/reconcile each publication boundary; preserve a proven rollback generation. |
| Read-only mapped Btrfs lowers, then read-only OverlayFS in upgrade:seed order; sibling/persistence restoration | S: sync `178-194,347-392`; bind `260-280` | Apply complete sync-style source/mode/identity observations to bind and running restoration. |
| Native idmap selection accepts current or next only when all present mappings agree | S: bind `126-150` | Reuse this rule in sync, which currently requires current alone (`211-217`). Do not start the guest to obtain current. |
| Running restoration is observation-only; stopped restoration invokes sync boot | S: `deploy/runit/libexec-3tched/restore-chatbot-root:74-109` | Verify full effective composition, not only overlay type/order/ro. Restore selected retained generation after interruption. |
| Boot selection preflights receipts and rejects duplicate logical identity selections | S: `deploy/runit/identity-roots/run:76-126,156-180` | Integrate the owner's established receipt locations; preserve unrelated identities and readiness fencing. |

Concrete gaps already evidenced: sync uses the old pool/source FSID while bind/restore use newer pins (R: SourceChain `89-141`); bind checks replica type/FSROOT but not its live FSID against the receipt (S: bind `77-83`); sync retains intent on failure but rejects incomplete state on re-entry rather than reconciling it (S: sync `78-114`); publication uses two non-atomic renames (S: sync `340-344`); running restore checks only type/order/mode (S: restore `100-106`). These do not justify replacing the workflow.

The current binder is an initial-binding path: it expects `container-defined`, saves backups, edits fstab/hostname and can perform device preparation (S: bind `51-58,198-258`). **Do not replay that provisioning sequence against the owner's completed baseline.** Reuse its composition/verification part through the existing maintenance workflow, leaving the baseline's already established guest configuration and device contract intact.

## Minimum owner baseline handoff

Use one protected baseline receipt and its authoritative references, consumed consistently by all four existing components. This is an integration contract, not a new public schema, provisioning plan version or replacement Cozo record. Do not add fields to a strict receipt merely because this document lists them.

| Required fact | Minimum handoff evidence | Status here |
|---|---|---|
| Identity and native target | Existing caller/session binding reference, target name, native UUID, selected Incus project/remote, authoritative binding revision/operation reference and current stopped-state observation | Saved reports identify `3tchedCtlChatbot`, UUID `137c61ff-435c-4300-b3c0-c605e461be13`; preserve, do not recreate. Fresh baseline confirmation awaits owner. No credentials required in this report. |
| Inherited root | Actual canonical mounted path and filesystem identity, subvolume ID/UUID for inherited `@`, mapped lower mount path, required mode and immutable-seed receipt reference | Await owner-produced paths and observations; do not substitute old pool constants. |
| Inherited siblings | Actual source path, FSID, subvolume ID/UUID and required mode for each of the six agent siblings, plus guest destinations | Names are source-established: memory, rules, shared, skills, soul, user. Current source makes shared/soul ro and the other four rw. Confirm baseline matches its authoritative contract; do not change it here. |
| Persistence | Actual host ordinary-directory path, owning FSID/subvolume, inode/device identity, ownership/mode and guest mount destination | Source contract: `@agent_user/persist`, root-owned 0700, separately bound at `/opt/run-mounts/persist`; actual source mount awaits owner. Not a new subvolume or overlay upper. |
| Upgrade source and destination | Actual mounted source/replica paths, each FSID and mount-root/subvolume identity, receive directory, publication location, owner/security modes and existing no-loop restoration contract | Await owner. Separate replica means distinct designated upgrade storage, not persistence or seed; no new partition/image/pool requirement is introduced here. |
| Retained upgrade chain | Current selected generation, host snapshot UUID, received snapshot UUID and Received UUID, published clone UUID/Parent UUID, read-only baseline properties, retained known-good generation and paths | Await owner's actual chain, or explicit evidence that initial pairing has not yet occurred. Never infer empty/unpaired state from a missing receipt. |
| Root/native/security integration | Native root path and pool binding, root-view/lower paths, exact idmap current/next observations, profile/device/security contract, lifecycle exclusion and helper closure references | Existing map is UID and GID namespace 0 → host 1000000, range 1000000000. Actual baseline readback and paths await owner. |
| Authoritative baseline completion | Receipt path/digest or immutable reference, existing operation/revision, terminal result and resulting authoritative identity/native state, boot restoration authorization and explicit power policy | Await owner. A local `root_bound` or `identity_registered` flag alone is insufficient. |

Mounted identity means exact mountpoint, filesystem type, FSID, mount root, expected subvolume identity and mode—not merely an existing directory or the nearest ancestor filesystem. Paths must be canonical, root-controlled and protected against symlink/rename substitution. Receipt paths, helper paths and receive directories stay protected. Existing authoritative facts are reused; final values must come from the owner, not this report's historical constants.

## Overlay and replication contract

### Layer composition

Conceptually, with paths supplied by the handoff:

```text
native root → read-only root view
               lowerdir = mapped_upgrade : mapped_inherited_seed_root
               no upperdir; no workdir
private persistence → separate rw bind at /opt/run-mounts/persist
agent siblings      → separate binds at /agent/{memory,rules,shared,skills,soul,user}
```

Map the Btrfs lowers before mounting OverlayFS, as the existing implementation does; do not attempt to idmap the overlay or recursively chown inherited data. Both lower exposures and the merged root are ro. The receive filesystem may remain writable, and the existing publication clone has subvolume `ro=false`; that is not a writable guest upper. No host writer may change a published lower while referenced by a mounted overlay. Received and source baselines retain the Btrfs **subvolume ro property**, not merely a ro bind mount.

Upgrade content has precedence. Files absent from a sparse upgrade fall through to seed; deleting a seed file requires the existing OverlayFS whiteout/opaque-directory semantics in the upgrade artifact. Absence alone is not deletion. Validate the effective merged mountpoints before binding any private data: an upgrade may not hide or redirect the agent/persistence mount locations. Do not repair directories through a mounted lower/view. Transport OS upgrade content only, never agent state or persistence; retain the existing rejection of unaccounted nested source subvolumes (S: sync `152-169,250-255,350-367`).

### Generation and ancestry

For generation G retain:

- Source snapshot H(G): actual source FSID, subvolume UUID, ro property and generation/transaction observations.
- Received baseline R(G): actual replica FSID, local subvolume UUID, `Received UUID == UUID(H(G))`, ro property and receive transaction observations where available.
- Published clone P(G): local UUID and `Parent UUID == UUID(R(G))`; source identity behind the mapped upgrade lower must be P(G).
- Logical generation label and predecessor, linked to the same native UUID and baseline receipt. A timestamp/name is only a selector, not proof. Local Btrfs transaction IDs are observations, not globally equal generation identifiers.

Before incremental send from G to N, verify both retained H(G) and R(G) are immutable, correspond by UUID and belong to this pair. Verify N's received identity before publication. A same-named snapshot is not a common baseline. Never toggle a received baseline writable, overwrite it or use the mutable publication clone as an incremental parent. Keep the source and receiver ancestry needed for the selected generation, rollback generation and any pending transition; no automatic garbage collection is introduced.

The existing completed PairReceipt is strict (`deny_unknown_fields`, S: sync `400-405`; R: BackendProof `292-319`). Preserve its accepted shape. Additional transition identities belong in the existing helper's protected recovery evidence/private journal, linked to that receipt and operation, not in Cozo provisioning proofs or arbitrary new PairReceipt fields. Physical ancestry must still be observed; JSON labels are not substitutes.

### Stopped activation

1. Under the existing maintenance/lifecycle exclusion, validate the authoritative baseline reference, native UUID/session, stopped state, idmap/security contract, source/replica mounts and current selected generation. Helper locks alone do not stop external lifecycle writers; if exclusive maintenance cannot be established, do not activate.
2. Persist a pre-effect intent naming predecessor, candidate and exact affected objects. Use protected exclusive staging, file persistence, atomic receipt publication and directory persistence as the existing commit protocol does. Reconcile an existing intent instead of issuing a fresh transition.
3. Preserve the source's detach discipline: detach only proven owned sibling/persistence binds, native root, root-view and lower binds; verify no retained lower references under the maintenance contract. Never lazy-detach or mutate a live lower. Recheck stopped UUID and mappings immediately before switching.
4. Revalidate the exact receive destination mount identity immediately before receive while exclusion remains held. A missing mount must fail closed—never receive into the host-root fallback directory. Protect the receive directory from concurrent writers. Observe complete pipeline success, received UUID and ro state before clone/publication.
5. Prepare P(N), verify ancestry, retain P(G) and both immutable baselines, and reconcile the two rename boundaries. No receipt claims N active merely because the receive or first rename succeeded.
6. Rebuild mapped lowers, ro overlay, all separate sibling/persistence binds and native root. Verify exact sources, FSIDs/subvolume identities, lower order, modes, native/view object equality, idmap and effective guest mountpoints. Preserve unprivileged/nonnested operation, storage ioctl denials, device allowlist, socket-origin identity and existing grants.
7. Persist terminal pairing/activation evidence only after full restoration and readback. An initial unbound pair is transport-complete, not root-bound or running. Start remains the existing separately authorized lifecycle operation; overlay synchronization must not start the guest or rewrite adoption state.

## Interrupted transition and rollback

Implement reconciliation **inside the existing helpers**, not a recovery daemon. Keep the original operation, candidate and predecessor. On timeout/disconnect, assume effect is unknown, not absent. Read current objects and mounts under the same exclusion before taking the single missing transition.

| Observed boundary | Required reconciliation |
|---|---|
| Intent persisted, no completed receive | Keep G selected. Match any candidate source/receiver objects to the intent. An incomplete receiver is not R(N), even if its name matches. Retain/quarantine it out of publication; removal/retry requires explicit exact-object maintenance authorization. Never blind-replay into it. |
| Receive complete, clone absent | Verify UUID/ro/ancestry and ownership; finish the existing candidate clone without resending. If provenance cannot be proved, retain evidence and leave stopped. |
| Clone present, old `@` still published | Verify candidate Parent UUID and current G identity. Continue the same stopped transition; do not allocate a new generation simply because the receipt is incomplete. |
| Old `@` moved, new `@` absent | Use recorded identities to locate retained G and candidate N. Complete the intended N rename or an explicitly selected rollback to G. Do not select by newest filename. |
| New `@` present, receipt still intent | Verify that it is P(N); finish mount restoration and terminal publication. Do not resend or rotate it again. |
| `restore-intent`, partially mounted view | Inventory each existing mount. Keep correct owned mounts; detach/rebuild only proven owned inconsistent composition while stopped. An unknown reference or UUID mismatch blocks activation, not admission. |
| Fully restored root, terminal receipt publication uncertain | Re-observe full composition and candidate identities, then reconcile the same terminal receipt. Do not label error as no effect or clear the fence blindly. |

Rollback is an explicit stopped-instance selection of the retained **known-good** generation K, not an automatic error trap. `paired` proves transport/root restoration, not successful application behavior: the owner/lifecycle evidence must identify what is known-good. Retain K before activating N. Use the retained verified P(K), or reconstruct its publication clone from immutable R(K) if required, preserving exact ancestry. Rebind and verify the full root, then publish selection K using the existing receipt contract. H(K) and R(K) remain available for future incremental synchronization; do not leave `.generation` naming N while K is mounted. Never receive from or modify seed/persistence to roll back the OS.

Root rollback does not roll back private data. Any application data-format compatibility constraint remains visible in the generation's acceptance evidence; do not silently snapshot/reset persistence. If rollback compatibility or K's identity is unknown, retain both generations and leave the guest stopped for the existing owner to choose—do not invent a successful rollback.

## Boot restoration and narrow file changes

- **`sync-instance-upgrade.sh`:** consume owner-supplied mounted identity and receipt references instead of old hardcoded paths/FSIDs/image assumptions; leave backing restoration to the owner's established contract. No loop creation, member add/remove or format fallback. Retain send/receive, clone ancestry and detach logic. Add the phase reconciliation above, immediate pre-receive destination proof, consistent idmap selection and explicit retained-generation rollback within this helper's workflow.
- **`bind-instance-root.sh`:** integrate only composition and full source/mode/idmap verification with the completed baseline. Do not replay its initial fstab/hostname/device-preparation sequence. Require actual replica FSID and generation ancestry, and exact effective private binds before root-bound evidence. Guest configuration/security comes from the owner baseline; do not broaden it.
- **`restore-chatbot-root`:** consume the same established baseline and selected upgrade receipt. Running service restart remains observation-only with complete composition checks. Stopped restoration reconciles pending intent or restores the selected retained generation; no backing allocation or native recreation. A rollback selection must survive reboot. Do not unconditionally advance to host latest and undo it. The existing boot sync may advance only under the already authorized synchronization policy and a new explicit transition.
- **`identity-roots`:** preserve preflight of all selected receipts, duplicate-session rejection and no readiness on incomplete restoration. Restore the existing resources and verify the selected generation before readiness; do not suppress inherited/unrelated identities. Keep startup under existing power policy/authority. Host uses runit; guest systemd is separate. Base-service delivery remains distinct from application-helper staging (R: SourceChain `305-360`); no deployment is authorized here.

## Specified now; integration pending

Specified now: separation of transport/persistence, read-only layer precedence, UUID/ancestry invariants, mount identity checks, stopped activation, interrupted-publication reconciliation, known-good rollback and boot selection preservation. These reuse existing implementation rather than requiring another orchestrator.

Pending owner handoff: actual canonical paths, mounted FSIDs/subvolume identities and modes, completed baseline receipt/revision/native-state readback, no-loop restoration interface, retained generation chain/known-good selection, lifecycle exclusion and boot policy. Do not force those values to match obsolete pool constants. No claim is made that baseline provisioning, overlay integration or deployment has occurred.

## Verification and limits

Performed: bounded source/report reads; SHA-256 comparison of four current helpers against saved exports; three text diffs resolving the redaction-only differences. No program/helper execution, storage/native-runtime probe, build, test, smoke fixture, service action, provisioning or deployment. Future authorized operation evidence must show correct destination, receive/clone ancestry, full root composition, unchanged identity/security/persistence, interrupted-transition reconciliation, rollback selection and cold restoration; none is claimed exercised here.

Reused judgments: `../jev-seed-mechanism-correction.json` records the actual decisions `seed_plus_added_writable_member`, `no_requires_actual_topology`, `preserve_mechanism_investigate_no_loop`. The acknowledged panel receipt records one substantive response, one non-substantive response and three failures, **not consensus**. The correction is retained: seed backing, writable member, exposed subvolumes and upgrade replica are distinct; private writes are not an OverlayFS upper. No new JEV call or panel was made. Prior judgments do not approve this specification or prove today's baseline.

Coverage is focused, not full semantic review. R: SourceChain and BackendProof were reused; relevant NativeFeasibility sections and the incomplete HistoricalScripts report were reused. The latter ends mid-citation at line 137. Earlier partial CASE/manifest reads and unfinished corpus coverage remain partial; no packets, exports or completed reviews were regenerated. Prior findings are not current runtime receipts.

Separate replica means distinct designated upgrade storage, not persistence or seed; no new partition/image/pool requirement is introduced here. |
| Retained upgrade chain | Current selected generation, host snapshot UUID, received snapshot UUID and Received UUID, published clone UUID/Parent UUID, read-only baseline properties, retained known-good generation and paths | Await owner's actual chain, or explicit evidence that initial pairing has not yet occurred. Never infer empty/unpaired state from a missing receipt. |
| Root/native/security integration | Native root path and pool binding, root-view/lower paths, exact idmap current/next observations, profile/device/security contract, lifecycle exclusion and helper closure references | Existing map is UID and GID namespace 0 → host 1000000, range 1000000000. Actual baseline readback and paths await owner. |
| Authoritative baseline completion | Receipt path/digest or immutable reference, existing operation/revision, terminal result and resulting authoritative identity/native state, boot restoration authorization and explicit power policy | Await owner. A local `root_bound` or `identity_registered` flag alone is insufficient. |

Mounted identity means exact mountpoint, filesystem type, FSID, mount root, expected subvolume identity and mode—not merely an existing directory or the nearest ancestor filesystem. Paths must be canonical, root-controlled and protected against symlink/rename substitution. Receipt paths, helper paths and receive directories stay protected. Existing authoritative facts are reused; final values must come from the owner, not this report's historical constants.

## Overlay and replication contract

### Layer composition

Conceptually, with paths supplied by the handoff:

```text
native root → read-only root view
               lowerdir = mapped_upgrade : mapped_inherited_seed_root
               no upperdir; no workdir
private persistence → separate rw bind at /opt/run-mounts/persist
agent siblings      → separate binds at /agent/{memory,rules,shared,skills,soul,user}
```

Map the Btrfs lowers before mounting OverlayFS, as the existing implementation does; do not attempt to idmap the overlay or recursively chown inherited data. Both lower exposures and the merged root are ro. The receive filesystem may remain writable, and the existing publication clone has subvolume `ro=false`; that is not a writable guest upper. No host writer may change a published lower while referenced by a mounted overlay. Received and source baselines retain the Btrfs **subvolume ro property**, not merely a ro bind mount.

Upgrade content has precedence. Files absent from a sparse upgrade fall through to seed; deleting a seed file requires the existing OverlayFS whiteout/opaque-directory semantics in the upgrade artifact. Absence alone is not deletion. Validate the effective merged mountpoints before binding any private data: an upgrade may not hide or redirect the agent/persistence mount locations. Do not repair directories through a mounted lower/view. Transport OS upgrade content only, never agent state or persistence; retain the existing rejection of unaccounted nested source subvolumes (S: sync `152-169,250-255,350-367`).

### Generation and ancestry

For generation G retain:

- Source snapshot H(G): actual source FSID, subvolume UUID, ro property and generation/transaction observations.
- Received baseline R(G): actual replica FSID, local subvolume UUID, `Received UUID == UUID(H(G))`, ro property and receive transaction observations where available.
- Published clone P(G): local UUID and `Parent UUID == UUID(R(G))`; source identity behind the mapped upgrade lower must be P(G).
- Logical generation label and predecessor, linked to the same native UUID and baseline receipt. A timestamp/name is only a selector, not proof. Local Btrfs transaction IDs are observations, not globally equal generation identifiers.

Before incremental send from G to N, verify both retained H(G) and R(G) are immutable, correspond by UUID and belong to this pair. Verify N's received identity before publication. A same-named snapshot is not a common baseline. Never toggle a received baseline writable, overwrite it or use the mutable publication clone as an incremental parent. Keep the source and receiver ancestry needed for the selected generation, rollback generation and any pending transition; no automatic garbage collection is introduced.

The existing completed PairReceipt is strict (`deny_unknown_fields`, S: sync `400-405`; R: BackendProof `292-319`). Preserve its accepted shape. Additional transition identities belong in the existing helper's protected recovery evidence/private journal, linked to that receipt and operation, not in Cozo provisioning proofs or arbitrary new PairReceipt fields. Physical ancestry must still be observed; JSON labels are not substitutes.

### Stopped activation

1. Under the existing maintenance/lifecycle exclusion, validate the authoritative baseline reference, native UUID/session, stopped state, idmap/security contract, source/replica mounts and current selected generation. Helper locks alone do not stop external lifecycle writers; if exclusive maintenance cannot be established, do not activate.
2. Persist a pre-effect intent naming predecessor, candidate and exact affected objects. Use protected exclusive staging, file persistence, atomic receipt publication and directory persistence as the existing commit protocol does. Reconcile an existing intent instead of issuing a fresh transition.
3. Preserve the source's detach discipline: detach only proven owned sibling/persistence binds, native root, root-view and lower binds; verify no retained lower references under the maintenance contract. Never lazy-detach or mutate a live lower. Recheck stopped UUID and mappings immediately before switching.
4. Revalidate the exact receive destination mount identity immediately before receive while exclusion remains held. A missing mount must fail closed—never receive into the host-root fallback directory. Protect the receive directory from concurrent writers. Observe complete pipeline success, received UUID and ro state before clone/publication.
5. Prepare P(N), verify ancestry, retain P(G) and both immutable baselines, and reconcile the two rename boundaries. No receipt claims N active merely because the receive or first rename succeeded.
6. Rebuild mapped lowers, ro overlay, all separate sibling/persistence binds and native root. Verify exact sources, FSIDs/subvolume identities, lower order, modes, native/view object equality, idmap and effective guest mountpoints. Preserve unprivileged/nonnested operation, storage ioctl denials, device allowlist, socket-origin identity and existing grants.
7. Persist terminal pairing/activation evidence only after full restoration and readback. An initial unbound pair is transport-complete, not root-bound or running. Start remains the existing separately authorized lifecycle operation; overlay synchronization must not start the guest or rewrite adoption state.

## Interrupted transition and rollback

Implement reconciliation **inside the existing helpers**, not a recovery daemon. Keep the original operation, candidate and predecessor. On timeout/disconnect, assume effect is unknown, not absent. Read current objects and mounts under the same exclusion before taking the single missing transition.

| Observed boundary | Required reconciliation |
|---|---|
| Intent persisted, no completed receive | Keep G selected. Match any candidate source/receiver objects to the intent. An incomplete receiver is not R(N), even if its name matches. Retain/quarantine it out of publication; removal/retry requires explicit exact-object maintenance authorization. Never blind-replay into it. |
| Receive complete, clone absent | Verify UUID/ro/ancestry and ownership; finish the existing candidate clone without resending. If provenance cannot be proved, retain evidence and leave stopped. |
| Clone present, old `@` still published | Verify candidate Parent UUID and current G identity. Continue the same stopped transition; do not allocate a new generation simply because the receipt is incomplete. |
| Old `@` moved, new `@` absent | Use recorded identities to locate retained G and candidate N. Complete the intended N rename or an explicitly selected rollback to G. Do not select by newest filename. |
| New `@` present, receipt still intent | Verify that it is P(N); finish mount restoration and terminal publication. Do not resend or rotate it again. |
| `restore-intent`, partially mounted view | Inventory each existing mount. Keep correct owned mounts; detach/rebuild only proven owned inconsistent composition while stopped. An unknown reference or UUID mismatch blocks activation, not admission. |
| Fully restored root, terminal receipt publication uncertain | Re-observe full composition and candidate identities, then reconcile the same terminal receipt. Do not label error as no effect or clear the fence blindly. |

Rollback is an explicit stopped-instance selection of the retained **known-good** generation K, not an automatic error trap. `paired` proves transport/root restoration, not successful application behavior: the owner/lifecycle evidence must identify what is known-good. Retain K before activating N. Use the retained verified P(K), or reconstruct its publication clone from immutable R(K) if required, preserving exact ancestry. Rebind and verify the full root, then publish selection K using the existing receipt contract. H(K) and R(K) remain available for future incremental synchronization; do not leave `.generation` naming N while K is mounted. Never receive from or modify seed/persistence to roll back the OS.

Root rollback does not roll back private data. Any application data-format compatibility constraint remains visible in the generation's acceptance evidence; do not silently snapshot/reset persistence. If rollback compatibility or K's identity is unknown, retain both generations and leave the guest stopped for the existing owner to choose—do not invent a successful rollback.

## Boot restoration and narrow file changes

- **`sync-instance-upgrade.sh`:** consume owner-supplied mounted identity and receipt references instead of old hardcoded paths/FSIDs/image assumptions; leave backing restoration to the owner's established contract. No loop creation, member add/remove or format fallback. Retain send/receive, clone ancestry and detach logic. Add the phase reconciliation above, immediate pre-receive destination proof, consistent idmap selection and explicit retained-generation rollback within this helper's workflow.
- **`bind-instance-root.sh`:** integrate only composition and full source/mode/idmap verification with the completed baseline. Do not replay its initial fstab/hostname/device-preparation sequence. Require actual replica FSID and generation ancestry, and exact effective private binds before root-bound evidence. Guest configuration/security comes from the owner baseline; do not broaden it.
- **`restore-chatbot-root`:** consume the same established baseline and selected upgrade receipt. Running service restart remains observation-only with complete composition checks. Stopped restoration reconciles pending intent or restores the selected retained generation; no backing allocation or native recreation. A rollback selection must survive reboot. Do not unconditionally advance to host latest and undo it. The existing boot sync may advance only under the already authorized synchronization policy and a new explicit transition.
- **`identity-roots`:** preserve preflight of all selected receipts, duplicate-session rejection and no readiness on incomplete restoration. Restore the existing resources and verify the selected generation before readiness; do not suppress inherited/unrelated identities. Keep startup under existing power policy/authority. Host uses runit; guest systemd is separate. Base-service delivery remains distinct from application-helper staging (R: SourceChain `305-360`); no deployment is authorized here.

## Specified now; integration pending

Specified now: separation of transport/persistence, read-only layer precedence, UUID/ancestry invariants, mount identity checks, stopped activation, interrupted-publication reconciliation, known-good rollback and boot selection preservation. These reuse existing implementation rather than requiring another orchestrator.

Pending owner handoff: actual canonical paths, mounted FSIDs/subvolume identities and modes, completed baseline receipt/revision/native-state readback, no-loop restoration interface, retained generation chain/known-good selection, lifecycle exclusion and boot policy. Do not force those values to match obsolete pool constants. No claim is made that baseline provisioning, overlay integration or deployment has occurred.

## Verification and limits

Performed: bounded source/report reads; SHA-256 comparison of four current helpers against saved exports; three text diffs resolving the redaction-only differences. No program/helper execution, storage/native-runtime probe, build, test, smoke fixture, service action, provisioning or deployment. Future authorized operation evidence must show correct destination, receive/clone ancestry, full root composition, unchanged identity/security/persistence, interrupted-transition reconciliation, rollback selection and cold restoration; none is claimed exercised here.

Reused judgments: `../jev-seed-mechanism-correction.json` records the actual decisions `seed_plus_added_writable_member`, `no_requires_actual_topology`, `preserve_mechanism_investigate_no_loop`. The acknowledged panel receipt records one substantive response, one non-substantive response and three failures, **not consensus**. The correction is retained: seed backing, writable member, exposed subvolumes and upgrade replica are distinct; private writes are not an OverlayFS upper. No new JEV call or panel was made. Prior judgments do not approve this specification or prove today's baseline.

Coverage is focused, not full semantic review. R: SourceChain and BackendProof were reused; relevant NativeFeasibility sections and the incomplete HistoricalScripts report were reused. The latter ends mid-citation at line 137. Earlier partial CASE/manifest reads and unfinished corpus coverage remain partial; no packets, exports or completed reviews were regenerated. Prior findings are not current runtime receipts.
"}
